meta.title: How Teach turns your build into a lesson
meta.subject: Teach
meta.one_liner: Run Teach after building something. It reads the work already in your chat and opens a short visual explanation in your browser.

story.title: A finished build can still be hard to explain
story.plain: The useful thinking is scattered across messages, decisions, mistakes, and fixes. By the end, the thing works, but the builder may not have one simple picture of what they made or why it works.
story.takeaway: Teach turns the trail of building into a mental model you can remember.

story.title: A saved teaching prompt for your coding agent
story.plain: Teach is installed as a skill or plugin. When you run it in the same conversation, it asks the coding agent to find the important story in that work and turn it into a short visual lesson.
story.takeaway: You do not explain the project again because Teach starts with the context already in the chat.

story.title: One command becomes one local page
story.plain: Teach follows a short path from your active conversation to a page in your browser. It checks project files only when the chat leaves an important gap.
story.takeaway: The finished page stays on your computer; Teach does not upload it to Google or another hosted service.

visual.title: What happens after you run Teach

steps.label: Run Teach
steps.detail: Typing $teach in Codex or /teach in Claude Code starts the saved teaching instructions in the same conversation.

steps.label: Read the build trail
steps.detail: The coding agent reads the conversation and checks only the files needed to confirm what happened.

steps.label: Find three answers
steps.detail: It distills the work into the problem, what you built, and how the result works from start to finish.

steps.label: Open the lesson
steps.detail: A small Python script combines that explanation with the Teach page and opens the local HTML in your browser.

technologies.name: Skill or plugin
technologies.explanation: A reusable set of instructions that tells your coding agent how to do a specific job—in this case, explain the build.

technologies.name: JSON
technologies.explanation: A simple text format Teach uses to keep the lesson's title, three-part story, and visual steps organised.

technologies.name: Python
technologies.explanation: The small program that checks the lesson data and joins it with Teach's page design.

technologies.name: HTML
technologies.explanation: The finished web page file your browser displays locally on your computer.
